segments.text: So how you doing, guys?
My name is Tyler.
I'm one of the co-founders here as well at SoCal Contractor Exchange.
And we're going to start here with one of the most important topics, which is going
to be our culture, right?
How do you define culture?
It's difficult to find the right words for it in most places, but very simply, culture
is an experience, right?
So how do you make sure that you're creating an experience and you're finding your way
into that experience, your place into that experience, right?
So we've made it very simple for you.
Our culture is built on four values, all right?
That's going to be accountability, support, camaraderie, and shared success, right?
And each of those pillars builds on the last, right?
So you can't have shared success if you don't have support or if you don't have accountability.
So what do they all mean, right?
So if we're going to start at pillar number one, which is accountability, accountability
is the base of everything.
Without it, nothing else works.
So that's knowing what to do and when to do it.
It's knowing what your job is.
It's knowing your scripts.
It's knowing what the expectations are.
It's knowing your results of your leads.
And again, holding yourself accountable, right?
You are accountable for your results.
If things aren't going the way that you want them to go, don't blame everybody else, right?
Because that's out of your control and you can't change what's out of your control.
So it needs to be your fault, right?
In order for you to be able to then change it.
So if you're holding yourself accountable and you're learning and you're doing what you're
supposed to be doing, then we move up to pillar two.
Pillar two is going to be support, right?
Support means that when you want help, when you need help, you can get it.
And you not only can get it, but you seek it out, right?
You're seeking out opportunities to learn more.
You're asking for help when it comes to, hey, somebody gave me this objection.
I really didn't know what to do.
Or somebody said this and I kind of froze.
What could I have done different?
Or, hey, my lead results lately have been this and I'm accountable for those.
What can I do to improve that, right?
Or you hit a certain level of success and you're like, how do I break through that level of
success, right?
That's where the support comes in.
Here at SoCal Contractor Exchange, we do operate on one main principle, an open door policy,
right?
Whether it's myself, Shai, or your field manager, we are always available for you to come in and
talk to us, no matter how big or small the question, problem, or compliment is, all right?
Once you have that, we move into camaraderie, right?
Because if you're holding yourself accountable and you're asking for help, chances are you're
doing pretty good, right?
You're finding success.
And now you're able to enjoy the job.
You're able to enjoy the people that you're working with.
You're having fun doing it, right?
It doesn't just feel like a job.
Reason being, if you're not doing well because you're not holding yourself accountable, you're
not asking for help, you're probably pretty miserable and you're not having a good time,
right?
So again, it's starting at those pillars.
So you are doing pillar one.
You are doing pillar two.
Well, now it's time for fun, right?
And now you're having fun.
You're having a good time with the team.
You're really great energy.
People look up to you.
Well, now we get to pillar four.
Pillar four is that shared success.
That's where when one person wins, we all win, right?
Everybody's in a good mood.
You walk into the office, you walk into that morning meeting, and you can feel the energy,
right?
It just vibrates through your soul that everybody's in a good mood.
Everybody's crushing it.
That's when the swag shop comes alive.
You see everybody rocking their gear.
You see the team barbecues and the team events.
People are playing basketball.
They're meeting up in the gym.
It's just like everybody is thriving, right?
That is how the culture is built.

I'm not really having a good time at work, right?
